# The device wrap's door, as KNOWN ANSWERS: env_key[k]'s ladder head, MASTER section 7's wrap KDF,
# and the eleven-octet envelope's binding, one row at a time.
#
# WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR. m1 task 14's door is the first production caller of XwingEncapsulate and
# XwingDecapsulate, and almost none of it is observable through a round trip: a sealer and an
# opener written by one author agree about the order of wrap_key's nine info elements, about which
# thirty two of the fifty six octets are the key, and about which octets of the envelope are bound,
# whatever those answers are. Every one of those mistakes returns well formed octets, round trips
# against itself, and is visible only to a second implementation. This file is what a second
# implementation checks itself against, and what this one is driven over by wrap_test.go.
#
# HOW THESE ANSWERS WERE OBTAINED, stated rather than claimed. They were computed by running this
# package. That is weaker than the eph-window table next door, whose answers were derived from the
# spec sentence first and confirmed against the code afterwards, and the difference is not papered
# over: what makes these rows worth anything is that wrap_test.go recomputes the KDF rows a SECOND
# WAY, from RFC 5869 written out in keyschedule_test.go over an info this file's own reader
# assembles from MASTER section 7's field list rather than from WrapInfo. So a row is held by two
# derivations that share no code, and only the shared INPUTS below are taken on trust.
#
# FORMAT. Whitespace-separated fields, one row per line. Lines beginning with # and blank lines are
# commentary. The first field is the row's name; what follows is named in the row's own paragraph
# below. All octet strings are lower case hex. Lengths are decimal.
#
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SECTION 1 -- THE INPUTS
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Two of them are too long to print and are given as a RULE plus a digest of the octets that rule
# produces, so a second implementation can build them exactly and check that it did:
#
#   ct_xwing         = 0x5a repeated 1120 times   (draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem's ciphertext size)
#   target_xwing_pub = 0xa3 repeated 1216 times   (the same draft's encapsulation key size)
#
# They are never parsed by anything below -- wrap_key's info takes both as LP-prefixed octets and
# the KDF never looks inside either -- so a fill byte is as good as a real key here and says so.
# The KEM's own construction is held against the draft's published vectors in
# testdata/vectors/rfc/xwing-draft10.json and is not restated in this file.
#
# ENV_KEY, SS, GROUP_ID and TARGET_ID are ascending runs so that a transposition of any two inputs
# is visible rather than symmetric.

INPUT_ENV_KEY          0102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f101112131415161718191a1b1c1d1e1f20
INPUT_SS               4142434445464748494a4b4c4d4e4f505152535455565758595a5b5c5d5e5f60
INPUT_GROUP_ID         2122232425262728292a2b2c2d2e2f303132333435363738393a3b3c3d3e3f40
INPUT_TARGET_ID        7172737475767778797a7b7c7d7e7f80
INPUT_CT_XWING_FILL    5a
INPUT_CT_XWING_LEN     1120
INPUT_CT_XWING_SHA256  7763f588a6a971767b4eb159f10df37e943c752fc115a383cefce105acd9707c
INPUT_TARGET_PUB_FILL  a3
INPUT_TARGET_PUB_LEN   1216
INPUT_TARGET_PUB_SHA256 5c992a27b2bf010a04891bdac9c3be6944f6600d3e6e63ef56c7ef90a6b492fe

# The envelope: u8(wrap_format_version) u8(target_type) u8(payload_type) u64(content_epoch).
#
# TARGET_TYPE AND PAYLOAD_TYPE ARE 0x01 HERE BECAUSE THIS FILE NEEDED AN OCTET, AND THAT IS NOT A
# CODE POINT. MASTER section 7 names both as gaps it does not fill -- "neither has a code point
# anywhere", and, in the clarification of 2026-09-19, "the domain is not the encoding" -- and
# target_id is in the same list with four candidate byte strings. A second implementation that
# reproduces the rows below has reproduced the CONSTRUCTION; it has not agreed with anybody about
# which octet a device leaf is or which a pq_secret payload is, because no document says. Open item
# MG-7 in messagegroup/OPENITEMS.md carries it.

INPUT_ENVELOPE_VERSION       01
INPUT_ENVELOPE_TARGET_TYPE   01
INPUT_ENVELOPE_PAYLOAD_TYPE  01
INPUT_ENVELOPE_CONTENT_EPOCH 7
INPUT_ENVELOPE_ENCODED       0101010000000000000007

# The payload, which is what MASTER section 7 puts inside aead_ct:
#
#   aead_ct plaintext = secret | LP(identity_pub) | sig
#
# with secret 0x11 x 32, identity_pub 0x22 x 32 carried under a four octet big endian length, and
# sig 0x33 x 64 -- 132 octets. The octets are fill because THIS DOOR DOES NOT BUILD THEM: task 14
# step 3 is blocked by open item M1-52, which leaves the signature preimage at 1,320 or 1,356
# octets with no document choosing, so nothing in this tree can sign a wrap yet. What the width
# buys is the sizing check in section 3: a payload of exactly this shape is what makes
# len(wrap_body) 1,289, which is the number MASTER section 8.2 publishes.

INPUT_PAYLOAD_LEN     132
INPUT_PAYLOAD_SHA256  5b71af2074e55a629bf6e9b533ad912774bb5c663a44b059420cd87a2f84c51e

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SECTION 2 -- env_key[k]'S LADDER HEAD
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# MASTER section 8.2's ruling of 2026-09-13 puts env_key[k] where the class key stands for every
# other record, and changes nothing below it:
#
#   record_key[0]         = HKDF-Expand(env_key[k], "sender/v1" | LP(leaf_index), 32)
#   key_body | nonce_body = HKDF-Expand(record_key[0], "rec/v1/body", 56)
#
# The exporter itself cannot be pinned here -- MLS-Exporter("URmessage/v1/envelope", "", 32) needs
# live MLS epoch state -- so ENV_KEY above stands in for its answer and what these rows fix is what
# this package does WITH an exporter output. The label is pinned separately, against MASTER's
# literal, in wrap_test.go.
#
# THREE LEAVES AND NOT ONE, and the third is 0xffffffff because LP(leaf_index) is four octets and a
# builder that wrote a varint there agrees with itself at every small leaf.
#
# FORMAT: LADDER <leaf index, decimal> <record_key[0]> <key_body> <nonce_body>

LADDER 0          8dc39d5684a112beff718f6a2a6b20283aeffffebc2aeb4fd29b47548e47532d 95b163b107b3d481da39920a8f4391025824feb562a8e5549ab54ef37641a73f 0a9d6f03869d25f9c4c007983be2ec606b1c7c5f2e13a38f
LADDER 3          74d369ef8f3d00a0a24bf69a5d5973b9087df94e063c14b317204d6a870522f1 a68671a00f8175e069eb7399625de40f1294c7a005e956fb33befb5c2c1d4765 40e31e66c67d7a19057f2c5339562d04c1c369abbbec1733
LADDER 4294967295 b3550e0a0e9bef490a629ab5a370d17d81f86daded1085ce2e9f890d2dfa0f90 7234c7661321b6ec709449d5febd670329112b5cd56e3cd0b58fb82ed4d2e6b5 da8b802c585c67098bf4374cadc6967f3bfca808481ea943

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SECTION 3 -- THE WRAP KDF AND THE SEALED BODY
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# MASTER section 7, adopted 2026-09-18 from red-team finding M-15:
#
#   prk                   = HKDF-Extract(salt = "URmessage/v1/wrap-salt", ikm = ss)
#   wrap_key | wrap_nonce = HKDF-Expand(prk, info, 56)                 // 32 key | 24 nonce
#   info = "URmessage/v1/wrap" | LP(group_id) | u64(epoch) | u8(target_type) | LP(target_id)
#          | u8(payload_type) | u16(alg_id) | LP(target_xwing_pub) | LP(ct_xwing)
#   hybrid_ct = u16(alg_id) | LP(ct_xwing) | LP(aead_ct)
#   wrap_body = wrap_envelope | hybrid_ct
#
# alg_id is 0x0014, MASTER section 7.1's registration for X-Wing, and it is inside the key as well
# as on the wire -- which is M-15's anti-downgrade half: flipping the two octets on the wire yields
# a different wrap_key and the AEAD fails, instead of the field being one nothing checks.
#
# aead_ct IS SEALED WITH NO ADDITIONAL AUTHENTICATED DATA. Spec A section 5.11 records that
# "aead_ct still has no stated AAD", and everything an AAD would carry is already inside wrap_key's
# nine elements. A second implementation that passed the envelope as an AAD would produce a
# different tag and would not reproduce WRAP_BODY_SHA256.
#
# THE SIZING IS A CHECK AND NOT A CURIOSITY. MASTER section 8.2 publishes 1,289 octets of
# wrap_body, 1,293 of the 4,096 rung once the LP32 body prefix is on it, and a 2,803-octet zero
# tail. Those three numbers fall out of the widths above and of nothing else, so an implementation
# that reproduces WRAP_BODY_LEN has agreed about every length prefix in the grammar.

INFO_LEN              2429
INFO_SHA256           133457e336c2992f0352c33f455a55d0a5d8a30756023c0f0ed874571b9e3249
PRK_SALT              URmessage/v1/wrap-salt
INFO_LABEL            URmessage/v1/wrap
ALG_ID                0014
WRAP_KEY              284eb08cecb572f58d59858f884454f9b2247f26e61714044d7f15513ef4a1ad
WRAP_NONCE            3a09c478382b958575d5e38d529d8a191d8b211eee6ac9c6
AEAD_CT_LEN           148
AEAD_CT_SHA256        ff006967a37bacdbf4a1742fc4a8637713aae9abc88f9e53740137827a5ffbc6
WRAP_BODY_LEN         1289
WRAP_BODY_SHA256      6025a1e357fddfad1acb205418db4b09292bd0fc9e40b4974c675cef0af3386b
WRAP_BODY_OCCUPANCY   1293
WRAP_BODY_RUNG        4096
WRAP_BODY_ZERO_TAIL   2803

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SECTION 4 -- THE FAILING DIRECTION: TEN OF THE ENVELOPE'S ELEVEN OCTETS ARE BOUND, AND ONE IS NOT
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# THIS IS THE ROW SET THAT MATTERS, and it is here for the reason the epoch-digest corpus carries a
# seed whose digest is valid for an epoch one past its keys: a door that answers "yes" is not the
# same thing as a door that answered the whole question.
#
# The wrap envelope travels in the clear, outside hybrid_ct and outside the KEM seal. MASTER
# section 7's nine-element info binds the content epoch, the target type and the payload type --
# ten of the envelope's eleven octets -- so an attacker who changes any of those ten changes
# wrap_key, and the AEAD refuses. The ELEVENTH octet, u8(wrap_format_version), is in no element of
# info at all. The only construction in the corpus that ever covers it is the body signature, whose
# preimage MASTER section 7 extends by LP(wrap_envelope) precisely so that the envelope is signed
# by somebody -- and that signature is task 14 step 3, blocked by open item M1-52.
#
# So TODAY, at this commit, a wrap whose version octet has been changed on the wire opens to
# exactly the payload it carried, under the same key, with no refusal anywhere. That is not a
# defect of this door; it is the measured consequence of shipping the door before the signature,
# and it is written down here so that nobody reads a green round trip as coverage of the envelope.
# Open item MG-7. m1 task 14 property 9's four-cell table calls this row 1 of four, and says the
# killing set there is the version octet alone -- reachable only behind the signature.
#
# HOW TO CHECK IT WITHOUT A KEM. Each row below flips every bit of ONE octet of
# INPUT_ENVELOPE_ENCODED, rebuilds info from the flipped envelope and hashes it. If the digest
# differs from INFO_SHA256 the octet reaches wrap_key and the AEAD is the authority over it; if the
# digest is EQUAL, nothing in the key covers that octet. The verdict is stated per row so that a
# reader who disagrees with the arithmetic can see which claim they are disagreeing with.
#
# FORMAT: ENVELOPE_OCTET <index, decimal> <bound|unbound> <sha256 of info after flipping it>

ENVELOPE_OCTET 0  unbound 133457e336c2992f0352c33f455a55d0a5d8a30756023c0f0ed874571b9e3249
ENVELOPE_OCTET 1  bound   cca9b405e24110e928be6544cefeac7352448b070d1ee5445a8882a363dfd50e
ENVELOPE_OCTET 2  bound   bba056d90e9fbf04af6138ccd9ddb661315177a9f6b0a851175208eb095441f5
ENVELOPE_OCTET 3  bound   0800f8d7f51b74eadee88327b2be2b3a33aad99aff8806453735e74ba08b52a8
ENVELOPE_OCTET 4  bound   6a710a648ac18394ac45f841ed767c2a3befb7352ba77a067a9f9fb5f82e20e2
ENVELOPE_OCTET 5  bound   8ec30553493e7a6e5320e6c13f9118714f96d178d89bda9deba0f15e8179f12c
ENVELOPE_OCTET 6  bound   07030acaf4cbbfdfba50bdd0ba1de9e4b573196879dcfa3b4c898cbb8fbfb051
ENVELOPE_OCTET 7  bound   a36aa64f47f3a72b1184d97a91acbd92c33eb667fc9a1c3c9558f245fbbecf39
ENVELOPE_OCTET 8  bound   a0402a747879ebeca803213417af2f21996cd8623376fa5354c7754437335701
ENVELOPE_OCTET 9  bound   30bf13b40914bbb218801b0372846753c703b7f3ff89c75af5a9b01466fceabf
ENVELOPE_OCTET 10 bound   77910bea4635d7c8b29f5e94f3b10c05bba72e116d366b02d0f7813b9523e831

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SECTION 5 -- THE OTHER FAILING DIRECTION: A GENUINE WRAP OF ANOTHER EPOCH IS NOT A TAMPERED ONE
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# SECTION 4'S TEN "bound" ROWS SAY LESS THAN THEY LOOK LIKE THEY SAY, and this section is what
# keeps a second implementation from reading them as more. Each of those rows edits an octet AFTER
# the seal: the sealer used one envelope, the wire carries another, the opener derives a key the
# sealer never used, and the tag fails. That is a DISAGREEMENT, and it is the case MASTER section 7
# means when it says "a receiver that derives the key from the envelope's own values and finds
# aead_ct does not open has detected the disagreement fail-closed".
#
# A WRAP OF ANOTHER EPOCH IS NOT THAT CASE. It is a wrap nobody edited. Its envelope and its key
# agree with each other -- differently from this file's rows, but with each other -- so it opens,
# and it opens to the payload it carries. The two rows below are exactly that: the section 1
# envelope with ONE field moved, and the H(info) each produces. Both differ from INFO_SHA256, which
# is the check -- a different key, not a broken one -- and a wrap sealed under either of them is a
# perfectly good wrap that the AEAD has no reason to refuse.
#
# WHAT A SECOND IMPLEMENTATION OWES, and it is not an octet: the opener must compare the carried
# envelope against the epoch it is restoring and the payload kind it asked for, and refuse a
# mismatch, BEFORE it honours anything. Nothing in section 3 or section 4 can check that for it,
# because the octets are correct in both directions. The second row is the one that bites soonest:
# MASTER section 8.2's two device wraps for one leaf at one epoch land at ONE wrap_target_handle
# and differ in u8(payload_type) alone, so an opener that does not compare will take pq_secret[k]
# and eph_root[k] as interchangeable -- and they are not: one is PERMANENT and one is EPH(5), which
# is what makes section 8.1's disappearing-message promise cryptographic.
#
# m1 task 14 property 4's headline is this section and not section 4: "a wrap for epoch n+1 does
# not open as a wrap for epoch n". In this package the comparison is three required arguments of
# OpenWrapBody -- u64(content_epoch), u8(target_type) and u8(payload_type), each a parameter with
# no default, because a caller can leave a struct field unwritten and cannot leave an argument
# unwritten -- and u8(wrap_format_version) is deliberately not a fourth: open item M1-54 leaves an
# unrecognised version unruled, so nothing here refuses on it and section 4's row 0 still says
# what it says.
#
# FORMAT: GENUINE_OTHER <the field that moved> <the eleven envelope octets> <sha256 of info>

GENUINE_OTHER content_epoch 0101010000000000000008 6b9d5b8456d9e3580036af5fb80bb9fbe1e84612f49ad2549ea1c39e9df142dd
GENUINE_OTHER payload_type  0101020000000000000007 6a56ddd657d76a55d178c3f92bed71b48adb307e46a933794e4d95122ac0e3a5
